text:
Mikhail Sergachev's minutes keep climbing. He's averaged over 26 a night across his last ten games, more than three minutes above his season pace, and played 28 against St. Louis on Thursday. For a Utah team that has dropped four straight (two in overtime), he's the defenseman Andre Tourigny leans on most.

The production is steady rather than spectacular: 20 points in 20 games, 15 assists, 11 on the power play. He's shooting 10.6% with 5 goals on 2.8 expected, so the goals will probably slow. Utah's on-ice luck with him is about neutral, though, and the Mammoth own 57% of the five-on-five expected goals when he plays, which is a strong number for a top-pair defenseman in heavy minutes.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his defending at the blue line last season: he stopped 17% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%. Evolving-Hockey was less impressed overall, ranking him 88th among defensemen. He's also become a footnote in the Kucherov rumors, with one report linking the Mammoth to his old Tampa teammate. What to watch: whether his play holds up under these minutes.
headline: Sergachev is carrying Utah's blue line
